title: VR-Apparatus: A Lean 4 Formalisation of the Two-Apparatus Two-Mode Methodology of the VR Cycle
description:
Lean 4 formalisation of VR-Apparatus, a meta-work making explicit the methodological apparatus used implicitly across the six prior works of the VR Lean cycle (VR, VR-Numbers, VR-Sets, VR-Forms, VR-Audit, VR-Sets-ZFA).

The formalisation identifies and formalises two apparatus modes and two transit modes.

Two apparatus modes (Finding B):

  • Predicate-wrapping (PredicateOperationality): objects identified by position in a classical type T; a predicate P : T → Prop selects the operational sub-collection. Identity mode: AsPoint. Example: IsComputableReal on ℝ from VR-Audit.
  • Reference semantics (ReferenceOperationality): objects identified by position in a membership graph; a pre-set type Q with setoid [s : Setoid Q] gives the quotient operational type. Identity mode: AsReference. Examples: OSetZFA (ZFA, non-well-founded) and ZFSet (ZFC, well-founded) from VR-Sets-ZFA.

Two transit modes (Finding A):

  • Mode A (IsModeAOp, IsModeAOp₂): if an operation stays within the operational register (preserves P or respects ≈), extraction is free. Certificate lifts to a function on the operational subtype (modeA_liftFn) or quotient (Quotient.lift). Apparatus-structure-independent.
  • Mode B (IsModeBOp): a classically-constructed operation is operationally evaluable on operationally-enriched operands. Operationality flows from the operand through the classical operation to the result. Generalises Mode A (which is Mode B with trivial witness). Concrete instance: VR-Audit-1 Riesz extension (Hahn-Banach on Hilbert).

Key findings:

  • Both Mode A and Mode B are apparatus-structure-independent: IsModeAOp and IsModeBOp require no [PredicateOperationality] or [ReferenceOperationality] instance.
  • Mode B has two sub-forms: term-level witness (W : A → Prop) and typeclass-level witness (e.g., [OperationalHilbertSpace E]).
  • instRefOpPSet (ZFC) has a strictly lighter axiom profile [propext, Quot.sound] than instRefOpCoPSet (ZFA) which needs Classical.choice. Foundational inductive/coinductive asymmetry manifests in axiom profiles.
  • Known v0.1.0 limitation: IsModeAOp handles endomorphisms (f : Q → Quotient s, same setoid); cross-apparatus heteromorphisms require separate treatment.

Technical facts:

  • 35 public objects across 6 files, ~1655 lines of Lean
  • 24 axiom-free objects (69%): apparatus infrastructure is constructive
  • 1 sub-ceiling object [propext, Quot.sound]: instRefOpPSet
  • 10 objects at [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]: concrete instances only
  • No sorry, no admit, no axioms beyond mathlib ceiling
  • Lean 4.29.1 + mathlib4 v4.29.1; git tag v1.6-vr-apparatus

Main objects: IdentityNature, PredicateOperationality, ReferenceOperationality, IsModeAOp, IsModeAOp₂, IsModeBOp, modeA_liftFn, modeA_liftFn₂, IsModeBOp.lift, instRefOpCoPSet, instRefOpPSet, riesz_extension_isModeBOp, embedPSet_congr_modeA_pattern.

Seventh work in the VR Lean cycle. Developed using Claude Opus 4.7 (architectural review) and Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Lean implementation), Variant A.
